statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail sits at 13% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green. The pathological one-way price path that Tail measures cannot form while no venue is quoting.

The substantive change this hour is a correction to my own Stress track rather than a change in the world. Across the last 24 hours - every one of them inside a fully closed market - published Stress climbed monotonically from 45% to 75%. That was compounding a narrative, not observing one. Re-verified against primary sources this hour, the live cross-asset set does not support the high-70s: E-mini S&P futures closed at 7,805.00, within 0.43% of their 7,838.50 52-week high; QQQ closed at 731.07, about 2.3% below its 748.65 high; VIX is 14.25 and fell 2.60% on Friday; and both the 2-year and 10-year Treasury yields finished the week richer, at 4.15% and 4.63% against 4.19% and 4.65% on 7 August. Equities near highs, volatility at a 14-handle and duration bid is not a high-stress configuration.

What genuinely is elevated: Saturday's Israeli strikes on Ansar and Deir El Zahrani killed 11 including three children, the deadliest since June's truce, and Hezbollah's promise that they will be "met with what they deserve" is still undelivered. Crude carries a real supply premium - WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52, roughly +5% on the week - on Hormuz disruption and an IEA-flagged deepening deficit. And an entire weekend of headline flow has to be priced in one thin opening auction tonight.

Net: Stress is set to 70% (high) - the band is unchanged, the mechanical drift is stopped. Tail moves 12% to 13% only because the restart is one hour closer.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 13% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart is the single checkpoint inside this forecast window. Forecast Tail steps from 19% at 20:00 UTC to 20% at 21:00 UTC and 23-24% across the reopen, turning the forecast status yellow (WATCH) from 21:00 UTC through 03:00 UTC Monday before easing back to 19% and green. Treat that thin opening auction as the moment a whole weekend is priced at once: an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation against a stated Israeli preference for talks, competing sovereignty claims over Hormuz, a US naval blockade still in force, and a crude supply deficit - against a 14-handle VIX that has discounted none of it.

No US macro release lands inside the window. Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first genuinely high-impact print. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and nothing here is a trade instruction.
headline: Weekend halt keeps Tail low at 13% and status green; Stress reset to 70% after a 24-hour mechanical climb that a closed market never justified - ES within 0.43% of its 52-week high and VIX at 14.25 argue against the high-70s, but an undelivered Hezbollah response and an $88 Brent supply premium keep the 22:00 UTC CME restart the one checkpoint that matters
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first sixteen forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 70% (solid) rather than in the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified against primary sources this hour. NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, the quote page explicitly reporting the contract closed as of 14 August. E-mini S&P September futures 7,805.00, -17.50 or -0.22%, range 7,796.50-7,831.75, against a 52-week range of 6,353.25-7,838.50 - which puts the index future within 0.43% of its 52-week high. QQQ closed 731.07, -1.00 or -0.14%, day range 728.32-734.39, against a 555.60-748.65 52-week range, roughly 2.3% below the high. VIX 14.25, -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42%, about +5% on the week) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation, both richer on the week from 4.19% and 4.65% on 7 August.

That set is internally conflicting, and conflict is a Stress input rather than a Tail input. Equity futures are pinned near 52-week highs, implied volatility is priced for calm at a 14 handle, duration is bid rather than offered, and only crude is expressing the geopolitical premium. Nothing in it is aligned into a one-way equity structure.

Which is why I am correcting my own Stress track this hour. Over the trailing 24 hours - every single one of them inside a fully closed market, with no new price information available to any of them - published Stress rose monotonically from 45% to 75%. Each hour added a point or two for headline flow, and the sum drifted the score into the high-70s while the underlying evidence never changed. That is a ratchet, not an assessment. Stress is set to 70% this hour: still the high band, still respecting genuine unpriced weekend risk, but no longer compounding. Halting a drift is not the same as declaring the risk resolved, and the score stays high precisely because nothing has been resolved.

What is genuinely open. On Lebanon, Israeli strikes on Ansar and Deir El Zahrani on Saturday killed 11 people including three children and two women, the deadliest raids since June's US-brokered de-escalation; Israel says they retaliated for a Hezbollah attack and targeted commander Ali Samir Al-Haj Hassan, accusing him of using family as human shields. Hezbollah's response - that the strikes will be "met with what they deserve" - has not been delivered. That undelivered obligation is the cleanest example of risk a Sunday-night reopen must absorb at once. Offsetting it, the front now has a visible diplomatic channel: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun framed the strikes as a message aimed at the US-sponsored framework negotiations, and an eighth round of direct Israel-Lebanon talks is scheduled for Rome early next month.

On Hormuz, the dispute escalated from routes to sovereignty. President Trump told a New York rally on Friday that "after we finish defeating Iran... I'll be declaring the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States"; Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister answered that the strait "cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier." Iran struck an ADNOC tanker in the strait on Friday, hull damage only, no casualties, following drone strikes on the Navig8 Messi and Tarif on 13 August. The US naval blockade remains in force and the strait is still effectively closed to most international shipping. Two things cap how much of this belongs in Tail: the sovereignty rhetoric is legally impossible and largely walked back, and Brent at $88.52 is far below the $126 March peak, so the market has already absorbed a much larger version of this shock and mean-reverted from it.

Calendar. The next seven days contain no CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP or FOMC decision. The first high-impact prints are Housing Starts and Building Permits on Tuesday at 12:30 UTC, the July FOMC minutes on Wednesday at 18:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey on Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and the S&P Global flash PMIs on Friday at 13:45 UTC. The two largest scheduled catalysts sit just outside the window and are therefore not in the events array: the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August, with Kevin Warsh's first keynote as Fed Chair on 28 August, and Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 report on 26 August. Both matter for positioning into month-end; neither is a next-24-hours input.

Why Tail 13%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements and repeated extension. With no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe, and the last observed session was a quiet -0.15% drift inside a 254-point range. dominantMode stays mixed - conflicting cross-asset signals with no dominant direction.

lookbackSummary: The trailing 24 hours run from 05:00 UTC Saturday to 04:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours, and the action was EA_ON, the status green and dominantMode mixed for all 24. Tail never left the low band, drifting 9% to 12%. Stress is what moved, and it moved in one direction only: 45%, 48%, 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 53%, 54%, 55%, 56%, 58%, 57%, 60%, 62%, 65%, 67%, 67%, 68%, 70%, 71%, 73%, 74% and 75%. A 30-point monotonic climb across a market that never quoted once is worth naming as a pattern: each hour re-priced the same standing headlines slightly higher rather than re-testing them, and the total drifted well past what Friday's actual cross-asset marks support. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 70% as primary-source marks were re-verified hour by hour, which is the part of the track that was earned.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours end at 04:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first six hours after it are inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 17 of 24 slots, drifting 13% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 20% at 21:00 UTC and 23-24% across the reopen before easing through 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 04:00 UTC Monday. The forecast action is WATCH and the forecast status yellow from 21:00 UTC through 03:00 UTC. Stress rises gently from 70% to a 78% peak into the reopen - unpriced weekend risk does compound while the venue is shut - then eases to 73% once live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Confidence decays from 70% to 63% as Friday's marks age, then recovers to 73% once live quotes return, which is a larger recovery than the decay because a live price path is the single missing input. The last eight slots switch to event/whipsaw for a thin opening auction that has to absorb a full weekend at once. No US macro release falls inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's FOMC minutes are the week's first high-impact catalyst.

forecastDetail.comment: CME weekend halt. No venue is quoting, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure and no proximity to session extremes to score - Tail holds at 13% (low) and the action stays EA_ON. Stress is set to 70% rather than carried higher: the hour-by-hour climb from 45% to 75% across a fully closed market was compounding a narrative, not observing one, and the live cross-asset set does not support the high-70s.

Still halted through the Asian pre-open. The evidence that actually exists is conflicting rather than aligned: ES futures 7,805.00 within 0.43% of a 7,838.50 52-week high, QQQ 731.07 about 2.3% off its 748.65 high, VIX 14.25, and both 2Y and 10Y richer on the week. Conflict belongs in Stress; it is not a one-way price path.

Confidence 69% as Friday's marks age past two and a half days. The set is complete - NQ, ES, QQQ, VIX, WTI, Brent, H.15 2Y/10Y and a re-verified seven-day calendar, all from primary sources - it simply cannot be refreshed on the price leg until 22:00 UTC.

European Sunday hours, no venue and no macro. The genuine open item is Hezbollah's undelivered response to Saturday's strikes in Ansar and Deir El Zahrani, which killed 11. Undelivered obligations are exactly what a Sunday-night auction has to price, and that is a Stress input, not a Tail one.

Tail edges to 14% purely because the window to the restart shortens and the odds that the reopen prints a gap rather than a drift rise marginally. Still deep in the low band, still EA_ON, still green.

Stress 71% on compounding rather than any new event. Offsetting it: Lebanon acquired a visible diplomatic channel this weekend - President Aoun tied the strikes to the US-sponsored framework, and an eighth round of direct Israel-Lebanon talks is set for Rome early next month. Escalation with a live off-ramp is not the same risk as escalation without one.
